newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australis shares suspended on merger.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australis shares suspended on merger.

text.p: Trade in the shares of pay television operator Australis Media Ltd were suspended at the company's request on Monday to allow the market sufficient time to absorb details announced late on Friday of a proposed merger between Foxtel and Australis.

Foxtel, a cable television joint venture between state-owned telecommunications group Telstra Corp and News Corp Ltd, announced on Friday it would take a controlling stake of Australis under the merger agreement.
Foxtel and Australis said Australis would effectively acquire Foxtel from Telstra and News in exchange for new shares in Australis.
After the issue of up to 1.66 billion Australis shares, News Corp and Telstra would own up to 66.5 percent of Australis and each appoint three of Australis' 10 directors.
Telstra said the agreement included arrangements for it to roll out cable past 2.5 million homes by the end of 1997.
The previous deal with News Corp had stipulated that Telstra pass four million homes.
Australis said the merger deal would provide it with additional minimum funding of A$294 million over the next 12 months.
The Australis/Foxtel merger was expected to be completed in November after meeting a number of conditions including due diligence examinations and regulatory approval.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, which rejected an earlier plan to merge Foxtel and Australis, said on Sunday industry conditions had changed since its earlier rejection.

Telstra said the new cable rollout arrangement would generate pre-tax cash outlay savings of about A$1.5 billion over the next four years and reduce the fees payable by the Foxtel business by A$300 million over five to seven years.

Foxtel has about 200,000 subscribers for its service compared to 110,000 for the satellite-based delivery system provided by Australis. The other key competitor, Optus Vision, has about 180,000 subscribers.
Analysts estimate the pay TV industry has lost more than A$2 billion in less than three years.
Foxtel and Optus Vision have also guaranteed their own rival rugby league competitions to provide programming, at an estimated cost of more than A$500 million.
Australis had accumulated losses of $735 million up to end-March and had called on major shareholders, including Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd for financial support.
News Corp said the merged entity would trade under the Foxtel name and deliver programming via cable, satellite and microwave dish.

The Australian government plans to sell one-third of Telstra later in calendar 1997 and the telecommunications carrier has been under pressure by analysts and fund managers to tidy up its operations ahead of the partial float.
